0|1ce072cbfd8dba46f117804850398e0b3040a541|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: nVMX: Check a single byte for VMCS ""launched"" in nested early checks
Nested early checks does a manual comparison of a VMCS' launched status
in its asm blob to execute the correct VM-Enter instruction
VMLAUNCH vs. VMRESUME.  The launched flag is a bool
of _Bool.  C99 does not define an exact size for _Bool
that is must be large enough to hold '0' and '1'.  Most
compilers use a single byte for _Bool
The use of 'cmpl' instead of 'cmpb' was not deliberate
result of a copy-paste as the asm blob was directly derived from the asm
blob for vCPU-run.
This has not caused any known problems
variables to 4-byte or 8-byte boundaries and KVM zeroing out struct
vcpu_vmx during allocation.  I.e. vCPU-run accesses ""junk"" data
happens to always be zero and so doesn't affect the result.
[1] https://gcc.gnu.org/ml/gcc-patches/2000-10/msg01127.html
